'''Muhammad Abdul Bari''' ({{langx|bn|মুহাম্মাদ আব্দুল বারি}}; born October 1953) is a [[Bangladesh]]i-born [[United Kingdom|British]] [[physicist]], writer, teacher, and [[community leader]]. He is a former secretary of [[Muslim Aid]], a former chairman of the [[East London Mosque]], and a former secretary general of the [[Muslim Council of Britain]]. He also served as the president of the [[Islamic Forum of Europe]] (IFE) in its early years when it was formed to organize Bangladeshi diaspora professionals in Europe. In addition to consultancy work, he has written for publications including ''[[The Huffington Post]]'' and [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]], and has authored numerous books.

He has been described as one of the most powerful Asian Muslims in Western Europe. In 2006, [[Time Out (magazine)|''Time Out'']] put him at #7 on its list of movers and shakers in London.<ref name="bbc1">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/5046970.stm |title=Profile: Dr. Muhammad Abdul Bari |date=5 June 2006 |work=BBC News |access-date=6 December 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/the-good-list-2006-414252.html |title=The Good List 2006 |date=22 September 2011 |location=London |newspaper=The Independent}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |date=28 November 2006 |title=London's 100 top movers and shakers 2006 |url=http://www.timeout.com/london/features/2307/10.html |magazine=Time Out London}}</ref> He has also been listed as a community leader in ''[[The 500 Most Influential Muslims]]''.<ref name="TheMuslim500">{{cite book |url=http://themuslim500.com/downloads/m500-2013-131112-low.pdf |title=The Muslim 500: The World's 500 Most Influential Muslims, 2013/14 |publisher=[[Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre]] |isbn=978-9957-428-37-2 |editor-last=Schleifer |editor-first=S. Abdallah |location=[[Amman]] |page=145 |access-date=13 September 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://themuslim500.com/profile/dr-muhammad-abdul-bari |title=Dr Muhammad Abdul Bari |website=The Muslim 500 |access-date=1 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151005053258/http://themuslim500.com/profile/dr-muhammad-abdul-bari |archive-date=5 October 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Early life and education==

Abdul Bari joined the [[Bangladesh Air Force]] in 1978, after studying at [[Chittagong University]]. He married in 1981 and left the Air Force the following year.<ref>{{cite book |date=2016 |title=Debrett's People of Today 2016 |publisher=Debrett's |via=[[Credo Reference]]}}</ref> After moving to the United Kingdom, he earned a doctorate in physics from [[King's College London]] in 1986 and joined [[Royal Holloway, University of London]], as a [[postdoctoral research]]er. There, he became involved in community work.

He began teaching after completing a [[Postgraduate Certificate in Education]] (PGCE) at King's College London in 1991. He spent five years teaching science at a secondary school in [[London Borough of Haringey|Haringey, London]],<ref name="mcb">{{cite journal |title=A voice for Muslims (Profile: Muhammad Abdul Bari) |url=http://www.mcb.org.uk/uploads/Physics-World.pdf |journal=Physics World |via=Muslim Council of Britain |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605080708/http://www.mcb.org.uk/uploads/Physics-World.pdf |archive-date=5 June 2011 |access-date=6 December 2008}}</ref> and joined the Tower Hamlets Education Authority as a special educational needs specialist in 1997.<ref name="bbc1" /><ref name="mcb2">{{cite web |url=http://www.mcb.org.uk/article_detail.php?article=announcement-552 |title=MCB News |date=4 June 2006 |publisher=Muslim Council of Britain |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060613214824/http://www.mcb.org.uk/article_detail.php?article=announcement-552 |archive-date=13 June 2006 |access-date=6 December 2008}}</ref>

==Career==

TELCO is now a branch of [[Citizens UK]] (CUK), an alliance of local community organizing groups in London, [[Birmingham]], [[Cardiff]], [[Milton Keynes]], and [[Nottingham]]. Abdul Bari is a member of CUK's National Council and advised CUK's Commission on Islam, Participation, and Public Life, which was created in September 2015 to confront rising [[Islamophobia]] since the [[7 July 2005 London bombings]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.citizensuk.org/commissioners |title=Commissioners |access-date=18 December 2016 |newspaper=Citizens UK}}</ref>

He served on the [[London Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games|London Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games Board]] (LOCOG), which was responsible for preparing for and staging the [[2012 Summer Olympics]].<ref name="london2012">{{cite web |url=http://www.london2012.com/about/the-people-delivering-the-games/the-london-2012-organising-committee/locog-board.php |title=LOCOG board (About us) |publisher=London 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070808155630/http://www.london2012.com/about/the-people-delivering-the-games/the-london-2012-organising-committee/locog-board.php |archive-date=8 August 2007 |access-date=6 December 2008}}</ref>

In 2014, he created the website ''Head2heart'' as a sociopolitical commenting platform, in addition to his business website ''AmanaParenting'', which provides parenting support and consultancy work.<ref name="amanaparenting">{{cite web |url=http://www.amanaparenting.com/?page_id=2 |title=About |website=Amana Parenting |access-date=30 April 2014}}</ref> He created a bilingual (Bengali and English) YouTube channel under the same ''AmanaParenting'' banner, in 2015 to advise on parenting in a pluralist society.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/user/amanaparenting |title=Amana Parenting |via=YouTube |language=en |access-date=3 January 2020}}</ref> In 2018, Dr Abdul Bari consolidated his two previous websites and now presents his thought leadership on various social, political and community topics as well as parenting services through his personal blog ''DrAbdulBari .''<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://drabdulbari.com/ |title=Home |website=Dr Abdul Bari |language=en-GB |access-date=3 January 2020}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
In the [[2003 New Year Honours]], Abdul Bari was appointed a member of the [[Order of the British Empire]].<ref name="bbc1"/> In 2005, he was made a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Arts]]. In July 2008, he was made an honorary fellow of [[Queen Mary University of London]].{{Citation needed|date= June 2022}}

The ''[[London Evening Standard]]'' listed him as one of London's 1,000 most influential people in 2009.<ref>{{cite news |date=5 November 2009 |title=The One Thousand: Faith & Philanthropy |url=http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/standard-home/article-23764962-the-one-thousand-faith-and-philanthropy.do |newspaper=Evening Standard |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111215114206/http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/standard-home/article-23764962-the-one-thousand-faith-and-philanthropy.do |archive-date=15 December 2011}}</ref> He was also recognised for outstanding achievement in Islamic affairs and community relations by ''British Bangladeshi Who's Who''. In 2013, he was included in the [[British Bangladeshi Power 100]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://bbpower-inspiration.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/Booklet-BBPower100-2013.pdf |title=British Bangladeshi Power 100, 2013 |year=2013 |work=British Bangladeshi Power 100 |page=5 |access-date=1 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150206145130/http://bbpower-inspiration.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/Booklet-BBPower100-2013.pdf |archive-date=6 February 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

The [[University of East London]] granted him an honorary doctorate in education in November 2012 "for his work as Secretary General of the Muslim Council of Britain from 2006 to 2010 and for his contribution to the cultural life of east London".<ref>{{cite news |last=York |first=Melissa |date=30 November 2012 |title=UEL honours Doreen Lawrence, Dr Muhammad Bari, and Tom Canning with doctorates |url=http://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/uel_honours_doreen_lawrence_dr_muhammad_bari_and_tom_canning_with_doctorates_1_1723012 |work=East London Advertiser}}</ref> In the 11th Muslim Awards Ceremony of ''[[The Muslim News]]'' in March 2013, he received the ''Iman wa Amal'' (Faith and Action) Special Award.<ref>{{cite press release |date=26 March 2013 |title=Eleventh Muslim Awards Ceremony recognises the very best of British Muslim Achievement |url=http://www.muslimnews.co.uk/pressreleases/press-releases/eleventh-muslim-awards-ceremony-recognises-the-very-best-of-british-muslim-achievement-2/ |website=The Muslim News}}</ref>

Abdul Bari was appointed deputy lieutenant of the Greater London Lieutenancy in July 2016.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://greaterlondonlieutenancy.com/about-us/our-people/deputy-lieutenants/|title=Deputy Lieutenants|newspaper=Greater London Lieutenancy|access-date=18 December 2016}}</ref>

==Views==
Abdul Bari has appeared in the British media to speak about Muslims in Britain, integration, and efforts to control the rise of fundamentalism among and against Muslims since the [[September 11 attacks|11 September 2001]] and 7 July 2005 attacks. While being a Board Member of London 2012
Olympic and Paralympic Committee he also made many appearances on international TV. He also spoke at many universities, public institutions and other organisations while he was head of the Muslim Council of Britain. 
In an interview with ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'', he linked the rise of Islamophobia to elements of the media and to some politicians. "Some police officers and sections of the media are demonising Muslims, treating them as if they're all terrorists — and that encourages other people to do the same", he said.<ref>{{cite news |last=Harrison |first=David |date=10 September 2006 |title=Media 'contributing to rise of Islamophobia' |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/1528485/Media-contributing-to-rise-of-Islamophobia.html |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |access-date=21 February 2017}}</ref>

He contrasted the one-dimensional portrayal of the Muslim population with the treatment of [[Catholic Church|Catholics]] in Britain in the 20th century: "We shouldn't say Muslim terrorists; it stigmatises the whole community. We never called the IRA Catholic terrorists."<ref name="telegraph10Nov2007">{{cite news |last1=Sylvester |first1=Rachel |last2=Thomson |first2=Alice |date=10 November 2007 |title=Dr Bari: Government stoking Muslim tension |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/1568881/Dr-Bari-Government-stoking-Muslim-tension.html |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |access-date=21 February 2017}}</ref> He argued that the British government's response to [[violent extremism]] had created tensions both within the Muslim population and between it and the rest of society, and warned of the consequences of poisoning people's minds against an entire community, as happened in [[Nazi Germany]] in the 1930s.<ref name="telegraph10Nov2007" />

Abdul Bari often writes about family and parenting, as well as social, political, and global issues, in ''[[The Huffington Post]]'' and ''[[Al Jazeera English]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Muhammad Abdul Bari |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/muhammad-abdul-bari/ |newspaper=Huffington Post}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Muhammad Abdul Bari |url=http://www.aljazeera.com/indepth/opinion/profile/muhammad-abdul-bari.html |publisher=Al Jazeera}}</ref> On parenting, he urges the involvement of both mothers and fathers, calling them the "grass-root leaders for every generation of newcomers on earth".

In April 2016, the propaganda magazine of ISIS (Daesh) published a hit list of Muslim leaders in the West calling to "Kill the Imams of Kufr (the infidels) in the West". His name was among five in the UK.<ref>{{Cite web |last=5Pillars |date=14 April 2016 |title=ISIS publishes 'hit list' of British and Western Muslim leaders |url=https://5pillarsuk.com/2016/04/14/isis-publishes-hit-list-of-british-and-western-muslim-leaders/ |access-date=15 June 2020 |website=5Pillars}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Abdul Bari's interests include reading and travelling.<ref name="bbc1"/><ref name="mcb"/> He speaks [[Bengali language|Bengali]] and English fluently and is married with four children.<ref name="bbc1"/>
